58  25-03-2026 (Court No. 8)
 Kole  266045  CRA (DB) 140 of 2025  with  IA No. CRAN 2 of 2025  In re: An application for suspension of sentence under Section 389  (1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure/under Section 430 (1) of the  BNSS filed on 03.09.2025 in connection with Frezerganj Costal  Police Station Case No. 78 of 2018 dated 15.10.2018 under Section 376(2)(i) of the Indian Penal Code and Section 6 of the  POCSO Act.

-And-  In the matter of : Ananda Das  .... Appellan  Mr. Mritunjoy Chatterjee,
 Mr. Arka Roy,
 Ms. Nazia Parveen,
 Mr. D. Adhikari,
 ...
For the appellant.

Ms. Anasuya Sinha,
 Ms. Trisha Rakshit,
 ....

For the Sta  Dictated by Arijit Banerjee, J:-
 Re : IA No. CRAN 2 of 2025

1. 
In spite of service nobody appears for the victim girls/defacto complainant.
2. The petitioner has been convicted under Section 6 of the POCSO Act and sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 20 years.
He says that he is in custody already for about seven years eight months as would be borne out by the detention certificate filed by the State in Court today.
He prays for suspension of sentence.
The petitioner says that he has been falsely implicated.
The medical evidence does not support the prosecution case.
The complaint was lodged after undue delay without there being any explanation for the delay.
The petitioner has served a substantial portion of the term sentence of 20 years.
His prayer should be allowed.
3. Learned State Advocate opposes the prayer.
She says that the complaint was filed four days after the incident when one of the victim girls fell ill and divulged the incident to her mother.
The medical evidence corroborates the prosecution case.

Abrasions were found by the examining medical doctor in the private parts of the three victim girls who are aged about approximately 5, 6 and 8 years at the Ananda Das vs Unknown on 25 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84867856/

point of time.
She says that the crime is of a heinous nature.
A pervert like the petitioner should not be shown any mercy.

She further says that given the kind of person that the petitioner is,
if enlarged on bail, he may repeat similar types of offences.
4. We have considered the materials on record and the depositions of the prosecution witnesses.
The two victim girls who were examined by the learned trial court have said more or less the same thing which fully supports the prosecution case.
The medical evidence prima facie also supports the prosecution case.

5. In view of there being prima facie incriminating material against the petitioner and keeping in mind the heinous nature of the crime, although the petitioner is in custody for a substantial period of time, we are not inclined to allow this application for suspension of sentence, at this stage.
6. CRAN 2 of 2025 stands dismissed.

7. All observations made in this order are prima facie and only for the purpose of disposing of this application for suspension of sentence and the same shall have no bearing on the hearing of the appeal.
8. Section is directed to supply urgent photostat certified copies of this order to the parties, if applied for, upon compliance of all necessary formalities.

IN Re: CRA (DB) 140 of 2025:
9.
From a departmental note dated February 5, 2026, we see that the department has received the trial court records.
We direct the department to prepare the paper book by the end of May, 2026.

10. List the appeal for final hearing on June 10, 2026, marked 12.30 p.m. ( Apurba Sinha Ray, J. ) (
Arijit Banerjee, J. )
